name: CA-31
label: Safe D

Cisneros's roughly eight-to-one fundraising advantage and large cash-on-hand edge

model.rationale: The district's eight-point Democratic lean, a favorable national environment, incumbency, and Cisneros's roughly eight-to-one fundraising advantage all point the same way, and prediction markets at 96 percent Democratic agree; with no polling to contradict the fundamentals, this stays a Safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Ching or a sharp shift in the national environment could narrow what is otherwise a wide gap.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
California's 31st District leans Democratic by eight points, and incumbent Gil Cisneros enters the general election with a decisive financial edge over Republican Eric Ching. Cisneros has raised roughly $830,000 to Ching's $97,000 and holds a cash-on-hand advantage of more than twenty to one, while outside spending in the race has been negligible. Prediction markets price the Democratic chance at about 96 percent.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals: the partisan lean, a favorable national environment, incumbency, and the money gap. Ching would need a markedly different national climate or a late infusion of resources to close a gap this wide. The seat remains a strong Democratic hold, with the absence of polling the main source of uncertainty.
